stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190 million for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in Series C funding, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The investment underscores the increasing demand for co-orbital security solutions as the Department of Defense ramps up its focus on space domain awareness. With the DoD's pull-through effect, True Anomaly is positioned to capitalize on the growing market for satellite defense.
stories.soWhat: In an era where space threats are becoming more sophisticated, True Anomaly's funding suggests that investors are betting on the military's need for enhanced security measures.

stories.head: L3Harris and Sierra Space team for missile-tracking satellites
stories.body: L3Harris and Sierra Space are collaborating to build 36 satellites aimed at expanding the U.S. missile-tracking network. This partnership highlights a significant shift in defense priorities, as the U.S. government increasingly invests in technologies to address emerging threats. The deal adds to the $15.4 billion European space budget increase, showing that missile defense is a global concern.
stories.soWhat: With both companies cashing in on defense budgets, this partnership reflects the broader trend of military spending driving innovation in space technology.

stories.head: U.K. prepares new space strategy amid competition
stories.body: The U.K. government is gearing up to unveil a new space strategy, likely in response to increasing competition from nations like the U.S. and China. This strategy aims to bolster the U.K.'s position in the global space race, with a focus on commercial partnerships and technological advancements. As the U.K. seeks to keep pace, the strategy's details will be closely watched by industry stakeholders.
stories.soWhat: If the U.K. wants to remain relevant in the space industry, it needs more than just a strategy; it needs a solid execution plan that attracts investment and talent.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
